title: Finite-type relative ampleness has a common very ample power
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $X$ quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $\mathcal M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Here $\mathcal M$ is $f$-ample when $f$ is quasi-compact and, for every affine open $V\subset X$, the restriction to $f^{-1}(V)$ is ample in the absolute sense of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Say that $\mathcal M^{\otimes n}$ is relatively very ample over $X$ if there are a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal E$ and an immersion $i:Y\to\mathbf P_X(\mathcal E)$ over $X$ such that $i^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal M^{\otimes n}$, with the projective bundle as in [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. Then $\mathcal M$ is $f$-ample if and only if $\mathcal M^{\otimes n}$ is relatively very ample for some $n\ge1$, equivalently for every sufficiently large $n$. Moreover, whenever $\mathcal N$ is relatively very ample for a quasi-compact morphism $g:Z\to X$, the morphism $g$ is quasi-separated, the evaluation map $g^*g_*\mathcal N\to\mathcal N$ is surjective, and the associated map $Z\to\mathbf P_X(g_*\mathcal N)$ is an immersion.

source.place: Tag 01VU, lemma-finite-type-ample-very-ample, using Tag 01VR, lemma-relatively-very-ample (especially clause (4) evaluation surjection and immersion), together with Definition 01VM.

proof.text: Given local very ample witnesses for a quasi-compact $g$, [lem-trf-local-quotient-evaluation] gives $F=g_*N$, surjective evaluation and the maps $\alpha_j$ with $q_j=\varepsilon g_j^*\alpha_j$. Apply [lem-trf-projective-quotient-comparison] to these data: the classifying map $r:Z\to\mathbf P_X(F)$ is an immersion and $r^*\mathcal O(1)\cong N$. This globalizes local witnesses; the one-member cover proves the moreover clause.

If $M$ is $f$-ample, choose a finite affine cover $(V_a)$ of $X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover]. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $f_a:f^{-1}(V_a)\to V_a$ is locally of finite type, and $f$ is quasi-compact. The ample restrictions $L_a$ therefore satisfy [lem-trf-affine-eventual-power-immersion]. Let $d_0=\max(\{1\}\cup\{d_a\})$ for its finitely many bounds. For each $d\geq d_0$, the local projective-space immersions are bundle witnesses by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. Step 1 globalizes them for $M^{\otimes d}$. For an empty cover $X$, and hence $Y$, is empty; the bound remains $1$.

Conversely, suppose $N=M^{\otimes n}$, $n\ge1$, is relatively very ample, witnessed by $i:Y\to\mathbf P_X(E)$ and $i^*\mathcal O(1)\cong N$. By [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry], $i$ corresponds to a surjection $q:f^*E\to N$. Set $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Sym}(E)$, with its quasi-coherent graded construction [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra]. The universal property [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] extends the adjoint of $q$ to a graded map $\mathcal A\to f_*(\bigoplus_{k\ge0}N^{\otimes k})$; its degree-$k$ formula sends a product $e_1\cdots e_k$ to $q(e_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes q(e_k)$. Adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] gives $\psi:f^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{k\ge0}N^{\otimes k}$. The degree-one surjection makes $U(\psi)=Y$, and the quotient geometry identifies $r_{N,\psi}$ with the original immersion $i$. As $f$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [lem-trf-graded-immersion-ample-criterion] implies that $N$ is ample over every affine open of $X$.

source.place: Tag 01VN (lemma-ample-very-ample), proof via Tag 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), (6) implies (1); Tag 01VU, reverse implication.

proof.text: For an affine $V\subseteq X$, set $T=f^{-1}(V)$ and $L=M|_T$. Step 3 makes $L^{\otimes n}$ ample. Thus $T$ is quasi-compact, and each $y\in T$ has a section $s$ of $(L^{\otimes n})^{\otimes k}$, $k\geq1$, whose nonvanishing locus is affine and contains $y$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Reassociate tensors: $s$ is a section of $L^{\otimes nk}$ with the same germs and nonvanishing locus, and $nk\geq1$. Hence $L$ is ample. Quasi-compactness of $f$ gives $f$-ampleness. Finally eventual very ampleness gives one positive exponent by choosing $d\geq\max(1,d_0)$; Step 2 proves the converse.

lean.statement: theorem relative_ample_very_ample {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [CompactSpace X] (M : Y.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] : (((QuasiCompact f ∧ ∀ V : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen V → ∃ hM : ((tensorPullback (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι).obj M).IsInvertible, @IsAmple (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme ((tensorPullback (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι).obj M) hM) ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧ IsRelativelyVeryAmple f (M.tensorPow n)) ∧ ((QuasiCompact f ∧ ∀ V : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen V → ∃ hM : ((tensorPullback (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι).obj M).IsInvertible, @IsAmple (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme ((tensorPullback (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι).obj M) hM) ↔ ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n → IsRelativelyVeryAmple f (M.tensorPow n))) ∧ (∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (g : Z ⟶ X) [QuasiCompact g] (N : Z.Modules) [N.IsInvertible], IsRelativelyVeryAmple g N → QuasiSeparated g ∧ Epi ((tensorPullbackSectionAdjunction g).counit.app N) ∧ ∃ hF : ((pushforward g).obj N).IsQuasicoherent, ∃ r : Z ⟶ (@SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData X ((pushforward g).obj N) hF).relProj, r ≫ (@SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData X ((pushforward g).obj N) hF).relProjHom = g ∧ @ProjectiveBundleQuotientGeometry.IsCanonicalMap X ((pushforward g).obj N) hF Z g N ((tensorPullbackSectionAdjunction g).counit.app N) r ∧ IsImmersion r)
